But glob uses dynamic import — it's only loaded when the Dashboard page is actually navigated to. In Inertia, only the current page component (MainPage) is loaded. So NavUser (via Dashboard) would NOT be loaded when viewing the main page.

But my BFS followed the `import()` in app.ts's glob which includes `import("/resources/js/pages/Dashboard.vue")` — that's a lazy/dynamic import, only triggered on navigation to Dashboard. So it's not part of the main page load.

So the key question: does the main page (`/`, MainPage.vue) load correctly? The graph walk shows MainPage.vue and all its components resolve fine (they were among the 102 OK). The only real failure in the main page's actual load path is... none. NavUser is only reached via Dashboard's lazy load.

In a real browser, `import.meta.glob` returns a map of functions. The actual `import()` is only invoked when the user navigates to that page. For the main page `/`, only MainPage.vue is invoked. So NavUser is NOT loaded on the main page.

So the main page (`/`) should render correctly. The Dashboard.vue page would fail to render, and the production build (`npm run build`) would fail.
